headline: Nigeria's one Ebola patient got better. Now zero cases.
summary: A Swiss woman, Nigeria's only Ebola case, was flown to Geneva on Monday with her husband after Nigerian doctors got her through the worst of it. She is stable and talking, but may still be infectious. Nigeria is still checking 52 contacts and now has no cases. In Kenya, 20 people left quarantine after 21 days with no symptoms.

cover_question.q: Is she cured, or just moved?

cover_answer: Better, not cured. She may still be infectious.
table_question: Should your passport decide which hospital you get?

5-7.script: A lady in Nigeria, a country in Africa, caught a very bad germ called Ebola. Doctors looked after her until the worst passed, like a fever breaking, and she was awake and talking again. On Monday a hospital plane flew her home to Switzerland. Nobody else in Nigeria has the germ now, and the grown-ups there are keeping watch.
5-7.why: One fever breaking, one plane. The germ stays an ocean away.
5-7.why_long: This age takes one vivid feature for the whole event, so the script gives them the fever breaking and the plane, and keeps the 52 contacts and Congo's deaths off the card. Cantor found this age fears harm it can picture, so the germ stays an ocean away. Expect "can I catch it?" No. It passes only by touching someone very sick.

8-12.script: A Swiss woman flew into Nigeria from Uganda carrying Ebola, its first case. Nigerian doctors treated her through the worst, then a medical flight took her to Geneva on Monday. Nigeria is still checking the 52 people she met, like a smoke alarm left on after the fire is out. It now has zero cases.
8-12.why: Flight in, treatment, flight out, 52 still watched.
8-12.why_long: This age is working out cause and effect and whether a rule runs to the end, so the script runs the chain: a flight in, the worst of it in Abuja, the flight to Geneva, and 52 contacts still checked after the count hit zero. The smoke alarm is the mechanism. Expect "so is it over?" In Nigeria, for now. Congo has 9,900 cases.

13-17.script: Is she cured, or just moved? Nigeria's only Ebola patient is stable and talking, and Switzerland flew her to Geneva because she is Swiss. Nigeria's health minister says she may still be infectious. Second: the flight came down to a passport. What does a Nigerian with the same illness get?
13-17.why: Better, and maybe still infectious. Then the passport.
13-17.why_long: A teenager can hold two true things: the patient is stable and talking, and Nigeria says she may still be infectious. The script hands them that pair, then a flight arranged because the couple are Swiss, and asks what a Nigerian with the same illness gets. Expect "would you take the flight?" Say what you would do.

5-7.a: No. It is far away, and it only passes by touching a very sick person. Washing your hands is plenty.

8-12.q: Why fly her away if she was getting better?
8-12.a: She is Swiss. Nigeria's doctors got her through the worst.

8-12.q: How do they know nobody else has it?
8-12.a: Not yet. 52 people near her are being checked for 21 days.

13-17.q: Is she cured, or just moved?
13-17.a: Better, not cured. Stable and talking, and maybe still infectious.

13-17.q: How bad is this outbreak really?
13-17.a: Congo: 9,900 cases, 4,800 deaths since May. The WHO: fastest-spreading ever.
